content: {"claim":"recover_json_object does not apply last-wins duplicate-key parsing to candidates in the fenced pool, so a later fenced object with repeated keys is skipped and an earlier fenced strict object wins.","expected":"The second fenced object, {\"b\": 2, \"b\": 3}, should be scoreable by resolving duplicate key b last-wins to 3, and because it is the last object inside a code fence when any fence holds one, recover_json_object should return {'b': 3}.","observed":"recover_json_object returns {'a': 1}: it tries the later fenced candidate, strict parsing fails, the fenced branch sets parsed=None and continues, then the earlier strict fenced object is returned.","reproducer":"recover_json_object('```json\\n{\"a\": 1}\\n```\\n```json\\n{\"b\": 2, \"b\": 3}\\n```')","source_basis":"A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable; the object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one.","execution_evidence":"none: no executable oracle","scope":"Fenced JSON objects with a repeated key when another scoreable fenced object is present.","uncertainty":"I assume loads_strict refuses duplicate keys, as documented by _loads_last_wins; if loads_strict accepted them, the second object would parse strictly and there would be no defect."}
